financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/3] SOURCE SECTION: Broadcom 10-K FY2025 (filed 2025-12-18), covering audit opinion, consolidated financial statements, and Notes 1–2 (Overview, Accounting Policies).

KEY FINDINGS:
1. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 3): Total on-balance-sheet debt of ~$65.1B ($3.2B short-term + $62.0B long-term), net debt ~$49B. Largely VMware acquisition-driven. Cash interest $2.67B in FY2025.

2. COST_OPACITY — Goodwill (severity 3): $97.8B goodwill = ~57% of $171.1B total assets. Qualitative impairment test leaves large headroom for management judgment. No impairment recorded.

3. COST_OPACITY — Intangible amortization drag (severity 2): $8.06B annual amortization from acquisition intangibles in FY2025 alone; $32.3B net intangibles remain — multi-year earnings impact embedded in P&L.

4. COST_OPACITY — SBC (severity 2): $7.57B SBC in FY2025 (~11.8% of revenue), growing rapidly (from $2.2B in FY2023). Masks true cash economics.

5. OTHER — Software revenue recognition (severity 2): $27B infrastructure software segment flagged as critical audit matter by PwC. Termination-for-convenience clauses create material judgment in upfront vs. ratable recognition; auditor noted "high degree of auditor effort."

6. No off-balance-sheet SPVs, VIEs, or project finance structures disclosed in this section. No private AI lab equity investments identified in this section (would appear in later notes on investments/non-marketable securities).

7. No NVIDIA, hyperscaler, or AI lab counterparty named in this section. Third-party fab dependency (TSMC likely implied) noted in policy text but not named.

[chunk 2/3] Key SIFI-material findings from Broadcom FY2025 10-K financial notes:

1. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 3): Total debt $67.1B, dominated by acquisition financing for VMware ($86.3B deal). In FY2025, Broadcom issued $14B of new senior notes across three tranches to refinance $13.6B of floating-rate 2023 Term Loans — reducing rate risk but sustaining gross leverage. VMware-assumed notes still outstanding ($5.75B).

2. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 2): AR factoring program has grown rapidly — $7.4B sold in FY2025 vs $4.0B in FY2023 (+86%). Classified as operating cash flows, inflating reported CFO. Non-recourse structure keeps off balance sheet.

3. COST_OPACITY (severity 3): Goodwill $97.8B (no impairment ever taken post-VMware); $71.8B sits in Infrastructure Software where revenue concentration and customer churn risk is highest. No tax deductibility.

4. COST_OPACITY (severity 2): Intangible amortization front-loaded at $20.4B over next 3 fiscal years — significant drag on GAAP earnings that masks underlying cash generation and complicates peer comparison.

5. EXECUTION_RISK (severity 2): 67% of contract liabilities ($13B balance) are subject to termination for convenience — meaning stated $33.3B RPO backlog is partially contingent. One major hyperscaler pullback could materially reduce reported backlog.

No equity investments in named AI labs or compute providers were disclosed in this section. No SPVs, VIEs, or JVs with third-party debt were identified in the extracted text. Seagate SoC acquisition ($600M) is operational, not a hidden structure.
[chunk 3/3] AVGO FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-12-18). Key findings:

1. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (Severity 4): Single unnamed customer = 32% of net revenue ($63.887B total) and 44% of AR. This is the most SIFI-material signal in this section. The customer is in the semiconductor solutions segment — widely believed to be Apple, though not named. Trending up from 21% (FY2023) → 28% (FY2024) → 32% (FY2025).

2. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (Severity 3): $67.12B total debt principal outstanding (post-VMware). $43.3B due after FY2030. FY2025 saw major deleveraging: $13.595B of 2023 Term Loans repaid and $4.882B senior notes repaid. But gross debt remains very high. Fair value $64.6B.

3. TAX HOLIDAY CLIFF (Severity 3): Singapore/Malaysia incentives reduced FY2025 taxes by $2.709B (~12% of pre-tax income of $22.7B). Singapore expires through Nov 2030, Malaysia expires FY2028. This is a material cliff risk.

4. SBC OVERHANG (Severity 2): $23.833B unrecognized SBC over 3.4 years (~$7B/yr) versus FY2025 net income of ~$23.1B. Two-Year Equity Awards granted in lieu of annual grants add complexity.

5. CAMT VALUATION ALLOWANCE (Severity 2): $1.321B new allowance triggered by One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 4, 2025). Signals legislative-driven deferred tax asset impairment risk.

6. CHINA REVENUE (Severity 3): $11.155B from China/HK = ~17.5% of revenue. Filing notes product may ultimately be sold in US/Europe, but geopolitical/export control risk is real.

No SPVs, VIEs, or off-balance-sheet entities were disclosed in this section. No named equity investments in AI labs or compute providers were disclosed. No capex commitments to specific named counterparties (e.g., NVIDIA, TSMC) were disclosed in this section — purchase obligations are small ($132M) and IT service agreements ($4.1B) are not counterparty-specific. The revolving credit facility ($7.5B) had zero drawn as of filing date.
